value.name: realizes she will face Whitfield with evidence alone
value.description: Asha understands that in the morning she will go to Whitfield's office carrying only what is on the desk, without Devin's words to back it up.
evidence: she understood that she would walk into Whitfield's office in the morning with what was on the desk and nothing Devin had said to confirm it

value.name: hesitates after locking the briefcase
value.description: After the briefcase is latched, Asha remains seated for a long moment, staring at the ticks in the margin and absorbing that they change nothing.
evidence: For a long minute after the latch clicked, Asha did not get up.
The three ticks in the margin of the pad sat where she had left them, plain in the lamplight, and she found that looking at them a second time did not rearrange anything.

value.name: chooses not to call anyone
value.description: Asha decides against reaching for the phone, signaling that she will not seek immediate help or confirmation.
evidence: she finally stood she did not reach for the phone on the corner of the desk

value.name: turns off the lamp
value.description: Asha switches off the lamp, leaving the briefcase as the thing she will carry into Whitfield's office.
evidence: She turned off the green-shaded lamp instead
the shape of the briefcase on the desk was still the shape she would carry into Whitfield's office in a few hours

value.name: reopens the pad to inspect the marks
value.description: Asha turns the lamp back on and opens the pad again, returning to the page with the three ticks.
evidence: Asha switched the lamp back on and opened the pad to the page she had closed over the pen.
The three ticks were still where she had set them

value.name: touches the final tick
value.description: She traces the last mark with her fingertip and studies the skipped ink, as if trying to understand what it means.
evidence: she found that turning the light on again had not been to check them but to put her hand on them.
She traced the last mark slowly with her fingertip, following the small drag where the ballpoint had skipped, and then lifted her finger and looked at the ink that had not transferred.
